ai.description: Kuhl's Wart Frog reaches 5–8 cm. It is brown or grey with a mottled underside. Key features include a broad, flat head, distinct skin folds, and prominent bony projections on the lower jaw.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Limnonectes kuhlii* is best identified by the presence of prominent, fleshy odontoid processes (bony projections) on the lower jaw, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Limnonectes kuhlii* inhabits rocky, fast-flowing streams within evergreen forests and moist deciduous woodlands, typically at elevations between 500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Kuhl's Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits parental care, with males often guarding egg clutches in shallow water to protect them from predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Limnonectes kuhlii* breeds in streams during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in submerged rock crevices or shallow nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: Kuhl's Wart Frog inhabits the Western Ghats and Northeast India, typically found in streams at elevations ranging from 200 to 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: *Limnonectes kuhlii* emits a low-pitched, pulsed "chuck" or "gurgle" call. It is typically heard near fast-flowing streams in rocky, forested habitats.
